title: Governors reshuffle of March 2026
text:
In March 2026, the President approved a reshuffle of Governors and Lieutenant Governors across nine States and Union Territories. The reshuffle came as C.V. Ananda Bose resigned as Governor of West Bengal. R.N. Ravi, who had been Governor of Tamil Nadu, was moved to West Bengal in his place.

Kavinder Gupta, who had been Lieutenant Governor of Ladakh, was appointed Governor of Himachal Pradesh. Vinai Kumar Saxena, previously Lieutenant Governor of Delhi, was appointed Lieutenant Governor of Ladakh, and Taranjit Singh Sandhu was appointed Lieutenant Governor of Delhi.

Retired Lieutenant General Syed Ata Hasnain was appointed Governor of Bihar, succeeding Arif Mohammed Khan. He took the oath of office on 14 March 2026, and the Bihar Governor's office lists him as the 43rd Governor of the State.

questions.q: Under the Constitution, before entering upon office a Governor takes an oath or affirmation administered by whom?
options: The Chief Justice of the High Court exercising jurisdiction in the State
The Chief Minister of the State
questions.explanation: Article 159: the Governor's oath or affirmation is taken before the Chief Justice of the High Court exercising jurisdiction in the State or, if he is absent, the senior-most available Judge of that Court. The Chief Justice of India, the President and the Chief Minister are not named in Article 159.

questions.q: What minimum age does the Constitution prescribe for appointment as Governor of a State?
questions.explanation: Article 157 provides that no person shall be eligible for appointment as Governor unless he is a citizen of India and has completed the age of 35 years.

statements: I. Article 239AA makes special provision for the National Capital Territory of Delhi.
II. The Legislative Assembly of Delhi can make laws on police and public order.
III. Members of the Legislative Assembly of Delhi are chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct. Article 239AA(2) provides for direct election from territorial constituencies. Statement II is incorrect because Article 239AA(3)(a) excludes State List Entries 1 (public order), 2 (police) and 18 (land) from the Delhi Assembly's legislative competence.

list2: A. Ordinance-making power of the Governor when the Legislature is not in session
B. Immunity of the Governor from criminal proceedings during the term of office
C. Appointment of the Governor by the President by warrant under hand and seal
D. Executive action of the State expressed to be taken in the name of the Governor
questions.explanation: Article 155 provides for appointment of the Governor by the President by warrant under hand and seal (C). Article 213 gives the Governor ordinance-making power when the Legislature is not in session (A). Article 361 gives the Governor immunity from criminal proceedings during his term (B). Article 166 provides that State executive action is expressed in the Governor's name (D).

questions.assertion: A Governor of a State may reserve a State Bill for the consideration of the President.
questions.reason: Article 200 of the Constitution empowers the Governor to reserve certain Bills for the consideration of the President.
questions.explanation: Both statements are true. Article 200 is the direct constitutional source of the Governor's power to reserve a Bill for the President, so R explains A. Courts have since limited how this power may be used, but the power itself exists.

statements: 1. The Chief Minister of a State is appointed by the Governor.
2. The Governor is bound to act on the advice of the Council of Ministers in every matter, without exception.
3. The Governor of a State shall not hold any other office of profit.
4. The Advocate-General for a State is appointed by the Chief Minister.
questions.explanation: Two statements are correct: 1 and 3. Statement 1 reflects Article 164(1). Statement 3 reflects Article 158(2). Statement 2 is wrong because Article 163(1) excludes matters the Governor must decide in his discretion, and Article 163(2) makes his decision on that question final. Statement 4 is wrong because Article 165 provides that the Governor appoints the Advocate-General.
